messages.author: d80ddcad37e764f7
messages.subject: Using layout with ggplot
parts:
Does anyone have any experience of using layout with ggplot - for example if I set a layout such as:
mylayout=layout(matrix(c(1,2,4,1,3,5),ncol=2),widths=c(rep(1/2,2)),heights=c(2/20,9/20,9/20))

Then it gets completely ignored when I call ggplot which just writes to the whole window rather than the part I was intending it to go on.

Thanks

Peter

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Using layout with ggplot
parts:
Peter,

You need to use viewport instead of layout. Have a look at section 8.3
of the ggplot2 book for some examples.

HTH,

Thierry

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Using layout with ggplot
parts:
Hi,

See also ?grid.layout (there is a note saying that layout is not
compatible with Grid graphics).

Note that with your particular example you could use
gridExtra::arrange() as follows,

library(ggplot2)
p0 <- textGrob("this is a title")
p1 <- qplot(1, 1, main="plot 1")
p2 <- qplot(1, 1, main="plot 2")
p3 <- qplot(1, 1, main="plot 3")
p4 <- qplot(1, 1, main="plot 4")

# library(gridExtra)
# http://code.google.com/p/gridextra/
source("http://gridextra.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/R/arrange.r")
arrange(p0,
arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, plot=FALSE), ncol=1, heights=c(2/20,18/20))


Best,

baptiste
